The row subgroup sum r and signed column subgroup sum c act on that representation. Definition5.14 fixes e=r*c; hence c acts first on column vectors. substantive_reconstruction.cancellation: For p>d nonempty rows, the first column has p positions in any tensor-basis filling. Pigeonhole gives a repeated label and a transposition tau inside that column fixing this particular word. Right multiplication kappa -> kappa*tau bijects the entire column subgroup and flips each sign. With the homomorphic action this proves c Q_tau=-c, so c v=c Q_tau v=-c v. Complex characteristic zero gives c v=0. Although tau depends on v, no common tau is needed: every basis vector is killed, so linearity proves c is the zero operator on the whole tensor power. Only then is r applied, yielding e=r*0=0. Its image is zero and therefore supplies no nonzero irreducible realization of that shape.
substantive_reconstruction.explicit_order_witness: For T=[1,2;3] and v=121, r=I+(12), c=I-(13). The transposition (13) fixes v, so rcv=0. In contrast rv=121+211 and crv=211-112, a nonzero difference of distinct basis words in dimension at least2. This checks both the candidate's sign and tensor-factor order. It does not refute the p>d theorem: in that excluded regime c has already been proved globally zero, so both products happen to vanish. Thus the answer correctly classifies the predecessor's defect as ambiguous order wording, not a false row-count conclusion.
